title: Google is about to roll out a new AI model. Employees say they're testing another that's way better.
key_facts: Google is preparing to release its Gemini 4 'Argon' model to the public.
Staff are internally testing a newer Gemini 4 version called Carbon, seen in documents and screenshots, on Google's internal coding platform Jetski in recent days.
One employee said Carbon 'feels like Opus 5.5' for coding, with the caveat that more testing is needed.
Google has tested a series of Gemini 4 models internally named Argon, Barium and Carbon; Barium-B was chosen to become the public Argon.
It could not be determined whether Carbon will be an update to Argon or a different Gemini 4 model, and Google is not guaranteed to release it.
Google announced Gemini 4 in late September and said Argon would first go to partners in its Fairwind Program, which tests cyber vulnerabilities, before a wider rollout.
Anthropic and OpenAI have pulled ahead among developers with models for complex engineering work.
quote_evidence: Most recently, employees have been trying a new version of Gemini 4 internally named Carbon, according to documents and screenshots seen by Business Insider.
The latest updates might close that gap, but Google is not guaranteed to release them.
One employee told Business Insider that Carbon "feels like Opus 5.5" for coding, referring to Anthropic's most powerful model for long-term agentic coding.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows Google trying to close the coding-model gap with Anthropic and OpenAI, based on staff impressions.
event_date: Internal testing in recent days before 9 Oct 2026; Gemini 4 announced late September 2026
notes: Single outlet, anonymous employees, unreleased model; Business Insider could not confirm what Carbon will become.
